scope: Fresh checks of the modern claims used in the novice revision. This supplements, and does not relabel, the section-level October 2 evidence register. No complete original Agriculture upload was accessible in this workspace.

sources.title: FiBL DOK trial
sources.extent: Official project description, history, location and systems compared.
sources.supports: Introduction of DOK as the long-term Swiss farming-system comparison run by FiBL and Agroscope; the German initials and 1978 start.

sources.title: The DOK Trial, FiBL 2024 dossier
sources.extent: PDF positions 9–11: NOFERT, plot design and fertilisation differences; positions 32–33: carbon sampling, concentration and stock. Relevant text read through the web tool; shell download failed with tunnel 403.
sources.supports: Repeated plots, management packages, NOFERT receiving 500/501, topsoil sampling and the scoped 12% carbon-stock result retained in lesson 22.
sources.boundary: No new preparation-specific efficacy claim; no claim of reading every underlying paper or the full dossier in this pass.

sources.title: Organic farming in comparison, FiBL 2024 fact sheet
sources.extent: PDF positions 1–6, particularly yield discussion at position 3.
sources.supports: Retained 15% mean organic yield difference over six rotation periods, with crop differences and limits. The course continues to attribute these summaries to FiBL.

sources.title: Demeter standard landing page
sources.extent: Certification explanation, annual inspection, language/version and national-application notices; official English PDF link.
sources.supports: Plain introduction to certification in lesson 21. The official linked English edition remains 2026.

sources.title: International Demeter Biodynamic Standard 2026
sources.extent: Cover; section 6.2 at actual PDF positions 69–70 and Appendix 8 opening at position 122.
sources.supports: Required preparation measures and scope versus Appendix 8 recommendations.
sources.boundary: The contents page lists different numbers. Existing course references use actual PDF positions and were retained. No rates or new operating instructions were added; no fresh whole-standard review is claimed.

sources.title: NRCS Soil Health
sources.supports: Biological/functional soil care remains distinct from Steiner's attributed etheric account.

sources.title: NRCS Soil Health Testing
sources.extent: Test properties, sampling and interpretation sections. Resolved from the current Soil Health page after the older shorter path failed.
sources.supports: Biological, physical and chemical assessment, with methods and sampling context.

sources.title: NRCS Soil Organic Carbon Stock Monitoring, CEMA 221, October 2024
sources.extent: Definition and monitoring scope on PDF positions 1–2; stock definition on position 6.
sources.supports: The retained distinction between three observation visits and a carbon-stock monitoring programme over years.
sources.boundary: Used for the measurement distinction, not as advice on current funding eligibility.

sources.title: FDA FSMA Final Rule on Produce Safety
sources.extent: Biological soil amendments of animal origin and stabilised compost sections.
sources.supports: Retained raw-manure contamination and validated-treatment boundaries. Burial, smell or a spiritual description do not establish produce safety.
sources.boundary: United States guidance remains explicitly labelled; no universal application interval or recipe added.

sources.title: EPA Integrated Pest Management Principles
sources.extent: Action thresholds; monitoring and identification; prevention.
sources.supports: Organism identification and actual damage precede proportionate management; presence alone does not require intervention.

sources.title: Oregon State University Extension: Vegetative plant parts
sources.extent: Roots, vascular cambium, leaves and vegetative propagation sections.
sources.supports: Brief ordinary-botany orientation in lessons 6, 9 and 17.

sources.title: Oregon State University Extension: Reproductive plant parts
sources.extent: Seed formation, seeds and germination sections.
sources.supports: Flower/seed orientation in lesson 6; no source passage is converted into a claim about Steiner's seed-chaos mechanism.
